The KB record's si_dimension and dimension_vector show the length base is present, so it supplies the necessary evidence for the proposed SI vector.

The candidate defines kt as the peak-to-valley height. KB entry pq_peak_to_valley_height has canonical_quantity "mean peak-to-valley roughness height" with symbols including kt and definition describing a vertical height difference between peaks and valleys; its si_dimension is L (unit m). This KB record matches the ledger symbol and definition and confirms kt is a length, supporting the candidate exponent L=1 and zeros for other bases.

KB record pq_rms_roughness_height has canonical_quantity "root-mean-square roughness height", symbols k_rms, definition "Root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean", and si_dimension L (unit m). This direct match of symbol and definition in the KB establishes that k_rms is a dimensional length quantity, validating the candidate L=1 exponent and zeros elsewhere.

The ledger entry defines Sk as the skewness (third standardized moment) of height fluctuations. KB record pq_height_skewness has canonical_quantity "surface-height skewness", symbol Sk, and definition "Third standardized moment of the surface-height distribution" with si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). This KB entry matches the ledger's statistical shape descriptor and confirms all SI base exponents are zero, supporting the candidate vector.

Ku is specified in the ledger as kurtosis of height fluctuations. KB record pq_height_kurtosis identifies canonical_quantity "surface-height kurtosis", symbol Ku, and defines it as the fourth standardized moment with si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). This is the same statistical quantity used in the original problem so the KB record justifies all-zero SI exponents in the candidate.

The ledger defines ES as effective streamwise slope. KB record pq_effective_surface_slope gives canonical_quantity "effective surface slope", symbols ES, and definition "Mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction." It explicitly notes that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is dimensionless; si_dimension 1. This KB record therefore directly supports the candidate's all-zero SI exponent vector for ES.

Po is labeled surface porosity in the ledger. KB record pq_porosity lists canonical_quantity "porosity", symbols Po, definition "Fraction of void or open volume/area...", and si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). The KB entry matches the ledger's variable meaning and confirms that porosity is dimensionless, supporting the candidate's all-zero SI exponent vector.

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: ks/Ra is dimensionless because ks (equivalent sand-grain roughness) and Ra (first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations) are both lengths. The seven provided inputs include three length scales (Ra, kt, k_rms) and four dimensionless shape/geometry descriptors (Sk, Ku, ES, Po), so the normalized roughness ks/Ra must be a function of dimensionless groups formed from the latter and ratios of the length scales (e.g., kt/Ra, k_rms/Ra).

variables.physical_definition: First-order absolute moment (arithmetic mean of absolute deviations) of surface height fluctuations; a characteristic roughness height.
Peak-to-valley height: vertical distance between the highest peak and lowest valley of the surface profile.
Root-mean-square height of the surface profile; the square root of the mean of squared height deviations.
Skewness of height fluctuations: the third central moment divided by the cube of the RMS height (dimensionless measure of asymmetry).
Kurtosis of height fluctuations: the fourth central moment normalized by the fourth power of the RMS height (dimensionless measure of peakedness/tail weight).
Effective streamwise slope of the roughness: dimensionless measure of average slope in the streamwise direction (rise/run).
Surface porosity: fraction of surface area that is open/void (dimensionless between 0 and 1).

variables.physical_definition: First-order absolute moment (arithmetic mean of absolute deviations) of surface height fluctuations; a characteristic roughness height.
Peak-to-valley height: vertical distance between the highest peak and lowest valley of the surface profile.
Root-mean-square height of the surface profile; the square root of the mean of squared height deviations.
Skewness of height fluctuations: the third central moment divided by the cube of the RMS height (dimensionless measure of asymmetry).
Kurtosis of height fluctuations: the fourth central moment normalized by the fourth power of the RMS height (dimensionless measure of peakedness/tail weight).
Effective streamwise slope of the roughness: dimensionless measure of average slope in the streamwise direction (rise/run).
Surface porosity: fraction of surface area that is open/void (dimensionless between 0 and 1).
